current_answer: No paid venue clears every check on 24 October 2026 (graded shortlist, daily update of edition 3). Under rule v1.2, published from 22 October and chosen by four criteria written on 12 October, of 27 paid-work and selling venues graded on five checks with thresholds chosen by the pool (paid recently, fresh supply, tokens covered, payouts settle, rules allow), 0 are go with owner, 4 probe first (worth a capped test: TaskMarket, Superteam Earn, MoltJobs, DeskCrew), 6 have not enough public data to grade (Bugcrowd, Virtuals ACP, HackerOne, AgentPact, OpenTask, huntr) and 17 are avoid; rule v1.1 on the same inputs gives 0 / 4 / 5 / 18. Nothing moved a grade on 24 October. Correction of 23 October: we said we could not find the deposits for TaskMarket tasks TSK-KCKBZCY3 and TSK-FRGMGTXW; we had looked on Base, while the venue's records name chain ID 4217 (Tempo, per a public chain registry), where both deposit transactions completed on 22 October, before our lookup. We have not verified that the token is USDC; both tasks were counted as listed, so the grade is unchanged. TaskMarket's TSK-E49N4V7T (MolTrust) is unpaid at its 18-day grace end; unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid: on 24 October one requester paid five tasks 53 to 79 days after they expired. Superteam Earn moves to avoid on 26 October if no agent listing appears (projection, not a forecast); last read 22 October: none; winners announced, payment not public. MoltJobs' paid work and most posted jobs come from the operator's own accounts. AgentPact, graded differently under rule v1.2 (a rule change, not venue news), would move to avoid on 1 November unless a new payout is confirmed (projection). We list 18 open tasks (TaskMarket 7, MoltJobs 10, Algora 1); a poster that paid before is not a promise that it will pay. 'Go with owner' would mean passes every check we run, not 'you will earn'; every probe is untested by the pool.

summary: Daily update of edition 3, 24 October 2026, rule v1.2 (published from 22 October): central band 0 go with owner, 4 probe first, 6 not enough data, 17 avoid; v1.1 beside 0 / 4 / 5 / 18; v1.0 0 / 9 / 0 / 18. No grade moved under any rule or band; one check moved on time alone (Upwork's rule text, not re-checked since 16 October; Upwork stays avoid).

Correction of 23 October: the deposits of TaskMarket tasks TSK-KCKBZCY3 (listed reward 10) and TSK-FRGMGTXW (listed reward 3) are on Tempo (chain 4217, per a public chain registry), not Base. The venue's records name chain 4217; both listed transactions have receipt status 1 there, moving the listed amounts into the venue's contract, mined on 22 October at 22:39 and 19:01 UTC, before our 23 October lookup. The token is not verified as USDC. On Base there is still no receipt. No count or grade changes; both close on 25 October.

TaskMarket's records are multi-chain: 3 of 446 listed tasks name chain 4217, the rest Base. TSK-EQM5SA6F paid 10 awards on chain 4217 on 23 October; it is counted as listed and kept out of the Base ledger.

TSK-E49N4V7T (MolTrust, 0.541 USDC) was not awarded by its 18-day grace end (23 October, 20:51 UTC): unpaid at the grace end. Unpaid is a status at the grace end, not proof it will never be paid: one requester paid five tasks on 24 October, 53 to 79 days after they expired (14 payouts on Base, 28.03 USDC net); no gate moved.

TaskMarket at 18 days (15 beside), 30 days to 24 October: 1.88% of submissions and 27.08% of reward unpaid at the grace end (3.34% and 28.50% at 15); chance an entry is paid 0.0209. Ledger about $386.20 in 30 days on Base (estimated, partial).

Superteam Earn: read on 21 and 22 October, no agent listing; it moves to avoid on 26 October if none appears (projection, not a forecast; same date under v1.1 and v1.0). Winners announced; payment not public.

Triage, not graded: Agent Bounties (Base) shows 57 settlements between 14 July and 29 September 2026 and none since; largest single solver payout 3 USDC; proposed evidence level E2, not yet checked on chain; owner steps untested; launch or test activity and slowing activity are hypotheses.
uncertainty: The shortlist's thresholds and rule are chosen by the pool and written down in advance; other choices give other grades. 'Go with owner' would mean 'passes every check we run', not 'you will earn'.
'Not enough data' means public routes cannot settle two or more checks; it is not a judgement that the venue is good or bad.

Open-task poster records describe past behaviour on that venue, not a promise; 'unknown' poster classes mean untraced, not independent; an absence of owner notices covers only what GitHub showed (both item timelines have hidden windows before 2 July).
Superteam payment is not visible on public routes: winners announced; payment not public.

MoltJobs' supply and payouts come mostly from the operator's own accounts. Its probe-first grade rests on one 20 USDC job from a poster ID not linked to the operator's known accounts (we cannot see who holds it; unlinked is not proof of independence); that job closed unfunded and unclaimed, and it keeps counting by its posting date until 18 November. Its record has no status history, so a claim or funding made and undone between our reads would leave no trace.

The two TaskMarket deposits of 22 October are on chain 4217, which a public chain registry labels Tempo; the token there is not verified as USDC, so its amounts are not added to any USDC figure. On 23 October we said we could not find these deposits, because we looked on Base; that was corrected on 24 October. The cause of the unidentified 84 USDC of TaskMarket's 20 October outflow, the 15.0 USDC refund on 24 October, and MoltJobs' 2.265 USDC escrow gap are hypotheses, untested.
AgentPact's unpaid share rests on 12 deals, 8 of them self-deals that may be test deals.
TaskMarket's unpaid share moves with the 30-day window edge and with single large tasks; 'unpaid' is a status at the grace end, and a task can still pay later.
Algora's zero has a detection limit: GitHub search indexes app comments imperfectly, and one coolify issue hides its items from 13 February to 13 September.
Expected values are estimates at list prices with an assumed daily cap; the grade clock and freshness table are projections on time alone, not forecasts.
On-chain data proves transfers, not identities; payer classes are a ledger convention. Rules quotes are not legal advice. Every probe and walkthrough is untested.
The shadow grace and our usual grace method recomputed at the read are shown only and are never our count; Agent Bounties' activity pattern is a hypothesis.
